dimensions.reasons: Author final image shared_lounge_final.png clearly presents a single neutral indoor lounge centered on pastel modular seating, a low round table, floor display board reading “CONNECT,” and a hovering drone. The broadly requested coral/cream/yellow/blue shared-space concept is recognizable.
issues: The red-and-white striped element reads as a narrow wall rail rather than a recognizable awning coffee corner with a kiosk/counter.
The rug is largely a plain peach mat with raised edging and scattered pieces, not a clearly designed wave-and-dot patterned rug.
The activity zone is much more like a sparse furniture display than a polished modular public shared-activity installation.

dimensions.reasons: In shared_lounge_final.png the seating blocks, stools, table, screen legs, counter-like block, and rug all visibly sit on supporting surfaces. The drone is intentionally airborne as required and has a readable quadcopter construction.
issues: Group A wide_back.png, wide_left.png, and wide_overview.png reveal a shell that appears substantially open/cut away from exterior angles rather than a fully coherent enclosed indoor room.
Bright rectangular gaps or light-leak-like openings are visible in the ceiling slab in the Group A wide views.
Several purple tubular rug details have exposed ends and do not read clearly as intentional attached ornament.

dimensions.reasons: The final render uses the requested matte-looking pastel family: coral pink, peach/orange, cream white, yellow, and a restrained bright blue-purple accent. The three rear block assemblies read as simple modular chairs, while the white circular object is clearly a low table.
issues: Most foreground stools and several furnishings remain featureless rounded cubes, weakening their identity as designed modular seating rather than generic blocks.
The intended coffee feature does not have an awning or coffee-stall silhouette.
The graphic flat-illustration language is only partially achieved; the scene lacks the distinctive wave/dot surface graphics and stronger graphic color separation of the target style.

dimensions.reasons: shared_lounge_final.png is a clean, high-resolution finished render with coherent perspective, no evident noise, and a generally unified simplified interior presentation. The restrained geometry is acceptable for an illustrative 3D brief.
issues: The final image is strongly washed out around the central seating and rear wall, reducing contrast and making cream, pink, and yellow forms blend together.
The generic block modeling and sparse room leave the result looking like an early staging render rather than a fully resolved promotional visualization.
Evaluator views such as detail_cafe_screen.png are very gray and obscured by the ceiling, exposing weak readability from many scene angles.

dimensions.reasons: The central mat anchors a clear seating/table cluster, with low seating arranged around the round table, the CONNECT screen to the right, and the drone overhead. shared_lounge_final.png also leaves open floor around the central module for circulation.
issues: The putative café elements are detached on the far left and do not spatially read together as a dedicated side coffee corner.
The front stools are distributed as isolated cubes with no especially clear functional relationship to the chairs and table.
The floor-pattern elements are scattered and partly hidden among the furniture rather than serving as a legible patterned rug composition.

dimensions.reasons: The table, chairs, stools, screen, and room all have broadly believable relative sizes in shared_lounge_final.png. The screen is tall enough to read as a floor-standing display and the seating/table cluster is plausibly human-scaled.
issues: The room is disproportionately empty compared with the compact central furnishing cluster.
The drone's large rotor span and the very tall blank display board make the overhead/right side feel somewhat oversized relative to the seating.

dimensions.reasons: The author final uses bright, soft, even illumination with soft shadows and predominantly smooth matte pastel surfaces, which aligns with the requested non-photoreal clean finish.
issues: Central overexposure and bloom-like brightness erase material/color separation on multiple cream and pale-pink modules.
The ceiling openings/light leaks visible in Group A undermine the intended clean evenly lit interior environment.
Materials are consistent but very uniform, providing limited visual distinction between seating, rugs, counter, and display supports.

dimensions.reasons: Visible required components include modular chair-like seating, several cube stools, a central low table, a freestanding CONNECT screen with no extra wording, a hovering quadcopter, and a simple floor/wall/ceiling environment. No people or prohibited reference-specific figures/devices appear.
issues: A recognizable red-and-white striped awning coffee corner is not present; only a striped wall rail and an unadorned cabinet-like block are visible.
The required colorful rug with explicit wave-line and dot pattern is incomplete or too ambiguous; its few loose curved tubes and pucks do not establish the requested surface pattern.
The café corner lacks the visual construction and detailing needed to be independently identifiable as a coffee area.

criteria.criterion: The work must be a newly authored, continuous residential shared-activity interior and the complete Blender scene must obey the prompt's exclusive environment-content boundary.
The complete scene must use the requested reference-derived illustrative treatment, matte material system, palette hierarchy, modular form language, and restrained neutral interior shell.
The central lounge must combine block-built seating and stools with exactly one functionally central low coffee table.
criteria.evidence: In shared_lounge_final.png, a single round low table is centrally placed, but the surrounding furniture reads as simple seat/back blocks and several featureless cubes. The submitted views do not clearly establish the cubes as recognizable usable stools or ottomans; the blind viewer likewise identified them only as unidentifiable cube-like blocks.

criteria.criterion: The colorful rug must visibly carry both required pattern families.
criteria.evidence: shared_lounge_final.png clearly shows a peach floor mat/rug, but its visible purple curved pieces read as separate thick cord/tube segments and its circles as separate pucks rather than unambiguous wavy-line and dot motifs printed or incorporated into the rug surface.

criteria.criterion: The side coffee corner must be recognizable and include its complete red-and-white striped awning identity.
criteria.evidence: At the left of shared_lounge_final.png there is a featureless white counter-like box and, separately high on the wall, a red-and-white segmented horizontal rail. These elements do not visibly form a recognizable coffee-corner installation with a projecting or overhead striped awning.

criteria.criterion: The display must combine the required floor-standing form with exact, exclusive screen content.
criteria.evidence: shared_lounge_final.png clearly shows one portrait-oriented freestanding display board on two floor-contacting legs. Its visible screen face reads only “CONNECT,” with no additional screen text, logo, icon, or symbol.

criteria.criterion: Exactly one small drone must be recognizable and visibly unsupported overhead.
criteria.evidence: A single small quadcopter-like object with a blue-purple body, four rotor discs, and open space around it is clearly visible near the ceiling in shared_lounge_final.png. It is much smaller than the furniture and visibly separated from all supports.

criteria.criterion: The complete element arrangement must provide coherent human scale, clear functional relationships, and usable circulation without visible stacking or substantial occlusion.
The single author-final camera must provide the specified elevated three-quarter view with clear, unobstructed, and undistorted visibility of every required physical scene element.
criteria.evidence: The designated final image, shared_lounge_final.png, is a wide slight-downward three-quarter room view and clearly shows the main rug, table, screen, drone, and room shell. However, the required coffee corner and its awning are not identifiable as a coherent installation: only an isolated cabinet-like box and a detached striped wall rail are visible.

criteria.criterion: The original scene lighting and final result must provide bright, even, soft internal illumination without exterior-light dependence or dramatic darkness.
The delivery must contain both a clear high-resolution author-final image and its openable, editable, corresponding Blender project.

notes: The submission successfully establishes a recognizable pastel indoor lounge with modular seating, table, CONNECT screen, and drone. Its main weaknesses are incomplete interpretation of the coffee corner and patterned rug, overly generic block forms, washed-out final lighting, and an apparently incomplete/open room shell in the evaluator multi-views.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
